title: Maximum Product Subarray

copy.A: @hook Maximum Product Subarray में सिर्फ maximum रखने से क्या छूटेगा? | Given array: minus two, three, minus four. | Non-empty contiguous subarray का maximum product चाहिए। पूरे array का product twenty four है।
copy.B: Brute force में हर start चुनो, फिर right end बढ़ाते हुए running product निकालो। | Three elements पर six ranges check होंगी। | बड़े array पर O of n squared work: वही factors अलग starts से फिर multiply होते हैं।
copy.C: अब सिर्फ maximum ending product रखने वाला shortcut देखो। | Three पर maximum three है। Minus four आया, तो three into minus four, minus twelve। | लेकिन पिछला minimum minus six था। Minus six into minus four, twenty four! उसे खोना गलती है।
copy.D: Negative से multiply करने पर order उलटता है: सबसे छोटा product सबसे बड़ा बन सकता है। | इसलिए maximum और minimum ending products, दोनों रखो। | Current value अकेली, old maximum into current, old minimum into current: इन्हीं three candidates से नया maximum और minimum चुनो।
copy.E: Minus two से शुरू: maximum और minimum दोनों minus two। | Three आया: candidates three, minus six, minus six। Maximum three, minimum minus six। | Minus four पर candidates minus four, minus twelve, twenty four। नया maximum twenty four; global best भी twenty four।
copy.F: Zero पर भी नई शुरुआत possible है। | Given array: minus two, zero, minus three. Answer zero है। | Minus two और minus three को select करके product six नहीं ले सकते: बीच का zero skip करना contiguous rule तोड़ेगा।
copy.G: हर element पर three candidates: O of n time, O of one extra space। | Brute force quadratic था। दोनों new states पुराने maximum और minimum से निकालो। | Minimum product को याद रखना कब useful होगा? Comment करो।

teaching.problem: Find the largest product of a nonempty contiguous subarray; [-2,3,-4] yields 24 from the entire input.
teaching.brute_force: For each start extend the right endpoint and update a running product, enumerating all six ranges for three elements in O(n squared) time.
teaching.bottleneck: Different starts reprocess overlapping factors. Keeping only the maximum ending product is also insufficient: it loses prior minimum -6, which multiplies by -4 to make 24.
teaching.optimization: Multiplication by a negative reverses order, so either prior extreme can become the next maximum or minimum. Every ending subarray either starts at current x or extends a prior ending subarray; compare x, old_high*x and old_low*x for both new extremes.
teaching.dry_run: For [-2,3,-4], high is [-2,3,24], low [-2,-6,-12], best [-2,3,24]. At -4 the candidates are -4,-12,24. [-2,0,-3] returns 0; skipping the middle zero is not a contiguous subarray.
teaching.complexity: Three candidates per element give O(n) time and O(1) extra space. All-ranges running-product brute force is O(n squared) time and O(1) extra space.
